about: Olujo is a young tequila house with a single, unhurried purpose: one añejo, made well. It was founded by entrepreneur Adam Weitsman with partners Larsa Pippen and Oliver Camilo, and launched in 2025 with master blender Alex Garcia. Before choosing a producer, the team visited more than twenty distilleries, settling on Fábrica de Tequilas Finos in the town of Tequila, Jalisco (NOM 1472), at the foot of the Tequila volcano. Their rules were simple: no diffuser, no shortened fermentation, nothing done for speed.

The agave is 100% Blue Weber from the mineral-rich volcanic soils of Los Altos, the Jalisco highlands, harvested at seven years or older. The hearts are slow-cooked in stainless steel autoclaves, crushed in a roller mill, fermented in stainless steel tanks with deep-well water and distilled twice in pot stills. The tequila then rests 18 months in American white oak, comfortably past the one-year minimum for an añejo, before it is bottled at 40% alcohol.

The bottle is part of the story. Rather than glass, Olujo chose a ceramic decanter, designed by the sculptor Ivan Venkov and made by Anfora, a century-old ceramics house in Hidalgo, as a nod to Mexico’s artisan tradition. In the glass, the house describes vanilla, toasted oak, chocolate and gentle spice, with the agave still clear underneath. It is meant first for sipping neat, and second for spirit-forward cocktails.
facts: 100% Blue Weber agave, Los Altos de Jalisco, 7+ years old
